title: Abu Dhabi warns the UK, and Haaland's escape clause

rumour.claim: Haaland won't stay if City are relegated

segments.say: TEAMtalk claims Erling Haaland won't stay at City if they're relegated.

visual.text: Haaland walks if City go down?

segments.say: We'll tell you how much of that holds up at the end. First, today's actual news.
Bloomberg reports Abu Dhabi has warned the UK government a harsh punishment could hit future investment.
The UAE has put over £30bn into Britain in five years, including plans for an Oxford to Cambridge tech hub.

visual.label: UAE investment in the UK, last five years

segments.say: And City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak met the Business Secretary two weeks before the verdict.
Etihad has hired Quinn Emanuel, dubbed the world's most feared law firm, while City, who deny wrongdoing, appeal.
But here's the twist. Manchester United are counting the cost.
The Express reports United reviewed seasons City pipped them, including the 2012 title, lost on goal difference.
And Pep Guardiola plans to be at the Etihad for the PSG game on 14 October, to back his old club.
Next, a sanction hearing and City's appeal. Neither has a date, so any punishment is still to come.
Rumour check on Haaland. His contract runs to 2034, and The Sun reports there's no relegation clause.

visual.text: Haaland walks if City go down

segments.say: A legal expert told Goal players might try to end contracts, but Haaland's camp is silent. Three out of ten.
Would Haaland really leave? Comment below, and follow for tomorrow's update.

caption: Man City 115 charges update, Day 5: Abu Dhabi warns the UK over investment. Bloomberg reports the UAE warned a harsh sanction could hit future investment; Etihad has hired Quinn Emanuel; the Express says Man Utd reviewed what City's breaches cost them. City deny wrongdoing and are appealing; the punishment is undecided. Rumour check: Haaland. Sources: Bloomberg, Guardian, The Lawyer, Express, Goal, The Sun.
